note: Ukraine's national spirits. The ones with `start` describe the situation on 1 January 2000 and cite sources; the others are granted by Ukraine's focuses and decisions. Values are gameplay estimates.

spirits.name: Post-Soviet depression
spirits.description: Through the 1990s the economy was in depression with hyperinflation, and output fell to about half that of the Ukrainian SSR.

spirits.name: Dependence on Russian gas
spirits.description: Ukraine buys its gas from Russia and carries most of Russia's gas exports to the European Union; Naftogaz and Gazprom dispute prices, transit fees and debts.

spirits.name: A foreign fleet in Sevastopol
spirits.description: Under the 1997 partition treaty, the Russian Black Sea Fleet leases bases in Sevastopol until 2017.

spirits.name: Breadbasket
spirits.description: Rich black-earth soils have long made Ukraine a breadbasket, and mineral resources industrialised the Donbas.

spirits.name: Fragile recovery
spirits.description: Growth has returned, but the hryvnia and the banks are still fragile.

spirits.name: Diversified gas supply
spirits.description: Gas comes from domestic fields and from the west through reverse flows.

spirits.name: A navy of its own
spirits.description: Ukraine's navy and coastal defences are rebuilt.

spirits.name: Decentralised state
spirits.description: Amalgamated communities run their own budgets.

spirits.name: Anti-corruption institutions
spirits.description: An independent bureau, a prosecutor and open procurement fight corruption.

spirits.name: European integration
spirits.description: Free trade and close ties with the European Union.

spirits.name: Eurasian integration
spirits.description: Close economic ties with Russia and its partners.

spirits.name: A nation in arms
spirits.description: Volunteers, territorial defence and a society organised for its defence.

spirits.name: Drone industry
spirits.description: Dozens of firms and volunteer groups build drones for the army.
